headline: Parliament passes law to replace RAB with SRB
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) will be formed under the police, replacing the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).
details: The National Parliament has passed a bill to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Response Battalion (SRB) under the police.
The new force, SRB, is designed to replace the functions of RAB, transitioning the security apparatus to a police-led structure.
The bill was passed despite objections from opposition members of parliament. Opposition MPs expressed concerns that the SRB could simply be a 'signboard change' for RAB.
Some opposition members argued that the new force should not merely be a 'change of clothes' for the existing structure, emphasizing the need for genuine reform.
During the session, MP Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Iqbal expressed that the RAB had been misused by the previous government.
The transition from RAB to SRB represents a major shift in the security and law enforcement landscape of Bangladesh.
caption:
RAB is gone. Parliament has passed a law to replace it with the new Special Response Battalion (SRB).

The National Parliament has passed a bill to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Response Battalion (SRB) under the police.

The new force, SRB, is designed to replace the functions of RAB, transitioning the security apparatus to a police-led structure.

The bill was passed despite objections from opposition members of parliament. Opposition MPs expressed concerns that the SRB could simply be a 'signboard change' for RAB.

Some opposition members argued that the new force should not merely be a 'change of clothes' for the existing structure, emphasizing the need for genuine reform.

During the session, MP Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Iqbal expressed that the RAB had been misused by the previous government.

The transition from RAB to SRB represents a major shift in the security and law enforcement landscape of Bangladesh.

headline: 70 foreigners detained in illegal casino raid in Chattogram
summary: Police raided an eight-story building in Khulshi, seizing over 50 laptops and foreign currencies from citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam.
details: Police detained 70 foreign nationals during a raid on an illegal casino operating out of an eight-story building in the West Jalalabad area of Khulshi, Chattogram.
The operation, conducted on Thursday afternoon, was based on secret intelligence. Officers raided multiple floors of the building to uncover the gambling operation.
Among those detained are citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam. Police are currently questioning the individuals to determine their legal status in Bangladesh.
Authorities seized over 50 laptops, various foreign currencies, and other equipment used to run the casino operation.
Local residents reported that foreign nationals had been frequently visiting the building for about a month.
Law enforcement agencies have stated they will provide more detailed information regarding the identities of the and the seized equipment after the operation is completed.
caption:
70 foreigners detained in a single raid on an illegal casino in Chattogram. Over 50 laptops and foreign currencies seized.

Police detained 70 foreign nationals during a raid on an illegal casino operating out of an eight-story building in the West Jalalabad area of Khulshi, Chattogram.

The operation, conducted on Thursday afternoon, was based on secret intelligence. Officers raided multiple floors of the building to uncover the gambling operation.

Among those detained are citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam. Police are currently questioning the individuals to determine their legal status in Bangladesh.

Authorities seized over 50 laptops, various foreign currencies, and other equipment used to run the casino operation.

Local residents reported that foreign nationals had been frequently visiting the building for about a month.

Law enforcement agencies have stated they will provide more detailed information regarding the identities of the and the seized equipment after the operation is completed.
